feature1.prompt: Feature 1: Refactor the deletion process to improve signal listener checks. When using the .delete() method in Django, an unexpected UnicodeDecodeError can occur due to fetching unnecessary fields. This feature requires encapsulating the logic for verifying if deletion signals (pre_delete and post_delete) are connected by moving that logic into a dedicated helper method. After the fix, when no signal listeners are present, the system should continue using the fast deletion path without extra field selection, ensuring that deletion proceeds as it did under Python 2 without triggering Unicode decoding errors.
feature1.hint_texts: Refactor the code by introducing a new method (e.g., _has_signal_listeners) in django/db/models/deletion.py that checks for connected pre_delete and post_delete signals. Update the can_fast_delete function to use this new helper method instead of checking the signals inline. Ensure that if signal listeners are present, the deletion logic remains unchanged so that the overall behavior of deletion is maintained.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/db/models/deletion.py; modify the new _has_signal_listeners method and update can_fast_delete (roughly around lines 116-142 in the diff) to use it.

feature2.prompt: Feature 2: Optimize the deletion process by selecting only the required fields. The current .delete() method fetches fields that are not necessary for performing cascaded deletions, leading to performance issues and potential UnicodeDecodeErrors when decoding unwanted fields. This feature focuses on modifying the deletion logic so that when no deletion signal listeners are connected, only the explicitly referenced fields needed for the deletion are selected in the SQL query. After the fix, deletion should avoid processing junk data and execute more efficiently, similar to the behavior observed prior to upgrading Python.
feature2.hint_texts: Optimize the collect method in django/db/models/deletion.py by adding a condition that, when no signal listeners are detected (using the refactored _has_signal_listeners method) and no select_related interaction is present, only the necessary (referenced) fields are selected via the only() method. Use Python’s itertools.chain to build the set of referenced fields. Ensure that if signals are connected, the normal full field selection is retained.
feature2.entrypoint: File: django/db/models/deletion.py; modify the collect function (starting around lines 220 in the diff) to conditionally use the only() method for field selection, and add the required import (from itertools import chain).

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features modify django/db/models/deletion.py, especially the deletion logic that interacts with model signals and field selection. The shared signal mechanisms (pre_delete and post_delete) and the overall deletion process are common ground for both improvements.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1 provides a refactored and centralized method for checking deletion signal listeners, which Feature2 will leverage to decide whether to apply the field selection optimization in the collect method. The integration must ensure that when no signals are active, the optimized query is used, and that when signals are present, the behavior remains as before.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on each feature must coordinate to verify that the changes in signal listener checking (Feature1) do not disrupt the conditions relied upon by the optimization (Feature2). They should align on test coverage and behaviors related to SQL query generation and error handling during deletion.
